label: Thomas Aquinas, Summa contra gentiles I.13: In an ordered series of movers and things moved, if…
locator: I.13 [14]: In an ordered series of movers and things moved
interpretation: Second proof that movers and things moved cannot go to infinity: in an ordered series (one moved by another 'according to an order'), when the first mover is removed or ceases to move, no other mover moves or is moved, because the first mover is the cause of motion for all the others; an infinite series has no first, so nothing would be moved. Read as the series principle only, not the whole proof. Aquinas presents the argument as Aristotle's, among proofs 'by which both philosophers and Catholic teachers have proved that God exists' ([1]). Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
